subject.title: Bug: Billing error (402) causes infinite retry death spiral for inline-apiKey providers (no backoff)

question: Should OpenClaw make inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` credentials participate in persisted provider-level auth/billing cooldowns and accept fail-closed behavior during cooldown windows?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes existing inline-key upgrade behavior and creates a provider-scoped cooldown identity that maintainers should explicitly accept.

options.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
options.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline keys receive the same billing/auth cooldown protection as profile-backed credentials while preserving healthy stored-profile fallback.

options.title: Keep profile-only cooldowns
options.body: Document auth profiles as the supported billing-backoff path and leave inline API keys as immediate-retry credentials.

options.title: Request narrower design
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers specify the exact cooldown identity, persistence, fallback, and recovery behavior they want.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
recommendation.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline keys receive the same billing/auth cooldown protection as profile-backed credentials while preserving healthy stored-profile fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current-main history across model auth, runner behavior, and adjacent auth resolution in the implicated files.
